claim: The payment page serves any invoice by its counting number with no sign-in, so access to an invoice is not tied to anyone's permission to see it.
Nothing states that the billing app checks, on each request, that the invoice it loads by number belongs to the user's company.
notes: The app adds company filters by hand. Per-invoice ownership enforcement is unspecified. Missing row-level security in the database alone is not a vulnerability.

claim: The only stated role control is hiding buttons in the pages; nothing states that the server checks the role on each request.
notes: A client-side control is stated and a server-side one is not.

claim: The billing app saves every field an invoice edit posts, so nothing states that the paid flag and the payout bank account are limited to the users allowed to change them.
notes: Saving every posted field supports mass assignment. Whether any role is held back from those fields is unknown.

claim: The description does not define what each role may do to which invoices, beyond naming an admin and a viewer role.
notes: The description states tenant membership and query filtering; it does not define the complete permissions of each role.

claim: The description does not define which invoice fields each role may read or change.
notes: The field-level half of V8.1.1. This does not show that no policy exists elsewhere.

claim: The edit handler accepts every field it receives rather than a list of fields each action allows.
notes: Stated outright; the same fact as V8.2.3 read as a coding defect.

claim: The supplied description documents asynchronous, serial PDF rendering but does not explain how it prevents excessive submissions from denying timely service to other users or tenants.
notes: Missing documentation of the protection strategy, not proof that every operational defence is absent.

claim: Users, admins included, sign in with a password alone.
notes: Stated outright: no second factor for admins or viewers.

claim: When a support agent acts as a customer user, the record names the customer user and not the agent who acted.
